basic_identification.full_title: Alternative Drinking Water Service Provision During a Crisis — Guidelines (आपदा के दौरान वैकल्पिक पेयजल सेवा प्रावधान — दिशानिर्देश)
basic_identification.sector_category: Environment and Ecology / Water Supply and Services (approved by the newly established Environment and Ecology Division Council and finalized by the Water Supply, Wastewater, And Stormwater Systems And Services Sectional Committee, EED 04, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Water Supply, Wastewater, And Stormwater Systems And Services Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard provides comprehensive guidelines, planning frameworks, and operational strategies on Alternative Drinking Water Service (ADWS) provision during a crisis. It covers any event or situation that disrupts a utility's normal piped water distribution and demands more than usual operational arrangements, establishing a unified emergency response framework for the general population, essential facilities (hospitals, schools), and temporary settlements (relief and evacuation camps).

revision_history.edition: First Edition (officially adopted as a new dedicated national code of practice to standardize alternative water service provision under the newly formed Environment and Ecology Department of BIS)

version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2026 standard (NIL on this copy).

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Technical Guidelines (Environment and Ecology / Water Services)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 19757:2026 is an operational guideline and code of practice rather than a physical consumer material, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its planning frameworks, 36-hour trigger rules, water-seal safety measures, and water quality quotas is highly recommended for municipal corporations, water supply boards (such as DJB or BWSSB), and state disaster management authorities (SDMAs). It is legally incorporated into public utility tenders, emergency water supply contracts, and disaster preparedness checklists across India to ensure public safety during water system failures. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Defines a water crisis as any natural, technical, or human-induced event that disrupts a utility's normal piped water distribution and demands more than usual operational arrangements or emergency structures to manage.

Mandates that where an operational interruption or breakdown in normal piped distribution exceeds or is projected to exceed 36 hours, the drinking water utility must immediately ensure Alternative Drinking Water Service (ADWS) provision.
Requires that all equipment, vehicles, pipes, and tanks mobilized for ADWS deployment consist only of authorized, thoroughly disinfected assets to prevent waterborne contamination outbreaks.

Alternative water must be supplied at a quota conforming strictly to the quantity norms of IS 17392 (Disaster Management in Drinking Water Utility) and the biological, chemical, and physical quality norms of IS 10500 (Indian Standard for Drinking Water).

Details the non-conventional use of existing distribution networks as an emergency approach, incorporating temporary standpipes, water tanker recharge into mains, and operating networks at lowered pressure.

Establishes independent Temporary Points of Distribution (TPDs) established independently of the network, requiring sites to be selected based on rigorous standards of hygiene, accessibility, load capacity, safety, and the needs of vulnerable users.
Mandates that utilities proactively model and pre-plan disruption scenarios, secure standby contracts, and maintain mobilization resource sheets before a crisis occurs.

Prescribes a structured communication plan for informing users and stakeholders both before and during a crisis, detailing ADWS deployment timings, distribution locations, and appropriate water hygiene behavior.

Approves ten specific implementation pathways for crisis water delivery: static water tanks, containerized water, bottled water, fixed water resources, automated water transaction machines, mutual aid from neighboring utilities, mobile treatment units, community water points, and rainwater harvesting.

Annex B provides mandatory practical guidelines on managing layouts for TPD sites and supporting vulnerable users with special needs (such as elderly, disabled, or isolated populations) during water collection.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 19757 : 2026 is the newly established national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for alternative drinking water service (ADWS) provision during crises. Formulated under the Water Supply, Wastewater, And Stormwater Systems And Services Sectional Committee (EED 04), this standard regulates emergency responses when normal piped water distributions fail. It mandates an immediate ADWS trigger if outages exceed 36 hours, requires using only sanitized assets, and enforces supply quotas aligned with IS 17392 (quantity) and IS 10500 (quality). It details existing network modifications and independent Temporary Points of Distribution (TPDs), site selection criteria for vulnerable users, and structured crisis communication plans to ensure public health and water security.
